open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct an explicit estimator of the unordered centered Gaussian component covariances for a growing number \(p+1\) of components and prove a permutation-matched operator-error tail \(T_n(\delta)\), together with primitive polynomial-sample conditions and a determination of whether perfect-surgery geometry reduces generic near-disjoint separation requirements.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen assumptions give only iid sampling, positivity of each weight, and population model membership. They impose no quantitative lower bound on mixture weights, no spectral upper envelope, and no pairwise component-separation margin. The qualitative handle in \(\texttt{def:mixture-estimation-handle}\) specifies neither a clustering algorithm nor a finite-sample theorem. Without those quantitative premises, rare components and arbitrarily close Gaussian components preclude a uniform growing-dimensional covariance tail.
open_obligations.attempted: The available route is projection followed by recursive clustering and effective-rank covariance concentration. Population characteristic-function separation proves identifiability but supplies no finite-sample cluster-label or covariance rate; generic Gaussian-mixture clustering bounds require explicit separation and weight assumptions absent from the frozen core. Perfect-surgery precision sparsity is useful only after sufficiently accurate component covariance recovery, and by itself has not been converted into a sample-level clustering separation bound.
